recipes.name: Cheesy Hashbrown Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (2 pound) package frozen hash brown potatoes, thawed
1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine hash browns, Cheddar cheese, condensed soup, sour cream, ½ cup melted butter, onion, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Transfer mixture to a 3-quart casserole dish.
Add remaining 1/4 cup melted butter and cornflakes to a saucepan over medium heat; stir gently until cornflakes are coated in butter.
Sprinkle cornflake mixture on top of casserole.
Cover casserole and bake in the preheated oven until hot and top is crispy, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Hashbrown Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Nothing beats this hashbrown casserole for pure comfort! Lots of Cheddar cheese and a crispy cornflake topping make this easy version irresistible.

review.reviewBody: Made both as written and with a small change. I like the cream of mushroom soup better than the chicken. I also omit the topping, just because I never seem to have crushed cornflakes, and it is perfectly fine w/o. Here's a tip on how to get it to mix better. Make sure hash browns are thawed as per recipe instructions. Pour melted butter/margarine over the potatoes and mix. Then add the cheese and mix. Lastly add the rest of the ingredients. It seems to mix faster and better for me this way. It does need the full hour to cook or your onions will be crunchy. I usually divide this in half between 2 smaller casseroles, eat one for dinner and freeze the other. Thanks for the great recipe! Update: 15/02/07 - Tried the suggestion of putting french fried onions on top instead of the cornflakes - absolutely awesome! Don't put in at the start though...put in last 10-15 min and cook uncovered (watch as they burn easily), I sprinkled some extra cheese on top with the onions and it was really good!

What I love about this recipe is its versatility. I browned a pound of sausage with the onion and added it to the mixture. Also since I only had half a cup of cheddar cheese, I shredded an additional cup & a half of processed cheese. I used mushroom soup instead of chicken, and I didn't have cornflakes, so nothing but a sprinkle of parmesan cheese went on the top. I also left off the additional 1/4 cup melted butter, and since the processed cheese is so salty, I only used 1/4 teaspoon salt. It was a delicious main dish and would make an excellent breakfast casserole. Our family of 3 had generous portions and only ate half the casserole. My husband, who never likes leftovers and is not crazy about anything in a casserole, loves the leftovers.

The only thing that I do different is to used crushed French's onions to the topping. It adds just the right flavor.
Edit. I started adding a small can of jalapenos to it. Adds a great kick and more grown up flavor.

I'm all for easy. I add 1/2 a packet of onion soup mix. Don't have to bother with the onion prep this way and the onion soup mix gives the potatoes a nice zippy taste. Everybody always asks what's in my potatoes. They know there's something extra, but can never figure it out. If you use the soup mix don't add any salt, it is not needed. Also I never use butter, the cheese adds enough oil. Plus I use fat free sour cream and heathy request cream of mushroom soup. I don't usually add any topping, but if I do fried onions are the preferred topping in my house.

We really enjoyed this casserole for a “breakfast dinner” with eggs and turkey bacon and sausage. I cut it exactly in half with authors ingredients except cornflakes. I did use another viewers method of mixing melted butter, then cheese before adding other ingredients and it went together easily. I baked 30 minutes and then added french fried onions and more cheese for 10 more minutes. Perfect in a 2 quart casserole! Thanks - will make again! Edit 7-17-25. My husband loves this recipe but he recently got out of surgery and was put on a diet. I was able to use reduced fat cheddar, low fat sour cream, and 50% reduced Campbell’s cream of chicken- he still loved it!

Love this recipe. Kids love it too. I’ve been a couple of adjustments over the years. I make a double batch so I can freeze one and instead of 2 cans of chicken soup, I add one chicken and one mushroom. I also cook a pack of bacon until crispy and add that to the casserole, substitute 1/4 cup of the cheddar for Parmesan and finally, everyone’s favourite, I swap out the cornflakes for frosties for that lovely sweetness. I cook for 45 mins, covered and then take off the foil and then add the buttered frosties and cook uncovered for another 15 mins.

Well, I would and do make this a little bit different. First…it MUST be plain Ore-Ida hash browns 32oz bag (dethawed) - NOT shredded hashbrowns. 2 cups of Shredded Sharp Cheddar Cheese. Yellow Onion - small diced, 1/4 to 1/2 of an onion depending on the size 16oz of Sour cream instead of 8 oz. 1 can of condensed Cream of Chicken soup. Salt and pepper (as above) Melt one stick of butter and add it to the mixture Mix all ingredients Use butter to grease the bottom/sides of 13x9 pan for the topping, crush your corn flakes and then mix in 1/2 stick of melted butter and top the casserole. Bake in a 350 degree oven for 1hr. Done. Blessed goodness!!! It is close, but the differences, though slight, make a lot of difference in taste. My family begs me to make these for all important family get together and most holidays.

I’ve been making this hashbrown casserole for years, and it’s always a hit! Most of the time I make a couple changes but it’s good either way. I brown a pound of breakfast sausage along with the chopped onion and omit the butter. Due to personal preference, I swap the cream of chicken for cream of celery. I almost always skip the cornflakes and just do cheese on top. This works well for breakfast, brunch and dinner!! Try it, you won’t be disappointed!!

Amazing! I loved the fact that I didn't need to use eggs. I also cooked my onions but for the basic recipe, I used what I had on hand: Cream of Potato and Cheese Soup then added French Fried Onions the last 10-15 minutes with a bit more cheese (I didn't have corn flakes)! I cooked it in 2 8x8 dishes for 30 minutes so I could freeze one - super yummy!!!
Can This be made without the can of cream of chicken soup ? Any substitutions?

I cut the butter by 1/2, added real bacon bits ( easier than frying up bacon and almost as good!_ and 1/2 of a little can of chopped green chiles ( great flavor boost, plus I did a bunch of green onions for color/flavor instead of the white onion, Came out perfect! We love it this way, I also skip the topping, just sprinkled a bit more cheese/bacon on top ...YUM!
Really loved it. I think in future ones the only tweak I'll make is to increase the amount of cornflakes on top because I really liked them.
Followed recipe no changes. It was great.

I've made this many times, with some important changes. People fight over it. No Corn Flakes. Please! I spread the cream of chicken soup on the bottom of the pan and remove the pieces of chicken. Just can't feature pieces of chicken in my potato casserole. Also use a fair sprinkling of granulated garlic. French fried onion rings? (shrug). Why not? better than corn flakes. The casserole will brown without either. Don't cover it! I make it in a pan and cut it in squatres. It really is delicious.
I did as others suggested, instead of cornflakes, I used the crispy fried onions crushed up on top. Yum! I also did not have an onion, so I used onion powder. Very delicious.
Super good! Excellent comfort side dish. Do not skip the cornflakes, they are the icing on the cake!
This was simple and a huge hit at our family Easter brunch. From age 7 to 86, everyone loved this savory dish. The butter coated cornflakes on top really made this cheesy potato recipe stand out.
I had been making this with hashbrowns squares. now I might find the potatoes cook better this way. Add some chopped ham and you have dinner or breakfast ..thank you
Loved having the 1/2 recipe option!! Came out perfect! Thank you!
We have been using this for Xmas breakfast for 10 years or more! People ask for it now, they love it that much!
